subject: Dedicated capacity: reservation fitment questionnaire and initial sizing
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@zenith-analytics.com>
To: procurement@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing + GPU mix for inference workloads

Hi Karthik / Redwood team,

Thanks for taking this RFI. We're preparing a committed capacity purchase and need a short questionnaire filled so our cloud procurement team can compare vendors. High level asks:
- Target throughput: we expect 1,000 - 1,500 QPS at peak across endpoints (chat + embeddings), average request = 85 tokens in/out.
- Latency SLA: p95 generation latency target <= 250ms for chat, embedding 50ms p95.
- Workload mix: 60% chat (13B-70B-family models), 30% embeddings (512 dim), 10% reranking/other (smaller models).
- Want recommended GPU family mix for a 12-month reserved pool, expected steady-state baseline with 2x burst capacity.
- Pricing bands: committed vs burst and how burst is billed.
- We will need a technical workshop to finalize slotting.

Attached is our workload profile spreadsheet. Can you fill the recommended sizing, GPU types, and assumptions? Also call out any tail-latency or KV-cache considerations.

Thanks,
Liam
Procurement Lead, Zenith Analytics
[Attachment: zenith_workload_profile.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@zenith-analytics.com>, Nora Singh <nora.singh@zenith-analytics.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood-inference.com, monica_patel@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-09-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing + GPU mix for inference workloads

Hi Liam / Nora —

Appreciate the clear profile. We've completed an initial pass and attached three artifacts: a filled questionnaire, a GPU fitment matrix, and three commitment scenarios (conservative / balanced / aggressive). Highlights below — full detail is in the attachments.

High-level assumptions (please confirm):
- Avg request payload = 85 tokens total (prompt + response).
- Peak concurrency required to meet 1,000–1,500 QPS = steady baseline ~600 QPS with 2x burst to 1,400–1,800 QPS. We modeled traffic shape from your CSV.
- Model families: 13B (quantized 4-bit), 34B (quantized 4/8-bit), and 70B+ (FP16/AMP or optimized FP8 where supported).

Recommended reserved pool (balanced scenario):
- 8 x NVIDIA H100 (80GB) nodes — primary for 70B+ chat models and highest throughput low-latency slices.
- 16 x NVIDIA A100 80GB nodes — target for 34B and mid-size models; good cost/throughput for quantized variants.
- 24 x NVIDIA L4 / A10G class (inference-optimized) — for embeddings and small reranking models.
- Autoscale/burst: allow additional 1.8x capacity on-demand (hourly metered) with immediate fallback to smaller quantized variants if hardware constrained.

Operational notes:
- With our runtime's continuous batching and prefix KV cache, we expect effective per-node throughput to be ~20–25% higher than naive single-request estimates; we included that uplift in the workbook.
- Tail-latency risk: 70B long-context sessions are the largest contributor. Recommend prefix KV caching for repeated system prompts and a separate slot pool for long-context (>2k tokens) sessions.
- Pricing: reserved commit discounts apply to baseline capacity (pool above). Burst is billed at an on-demand uplift (listed in commitment_scenarios.xlsx); we can tier burst pricing by sustained hourly usage.

Next steps: confirm the balanced scenario or indicate appetite for conservative/aggressive, and we'll schedule a sizing workshop to finalize exact node counts, SLAs, and contract pricing.

Attachments: zenith_rfi_completed.xlsx, gpu_fitment_matrix.pdf, commitment_scenarios.xlsx

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
[Attachment: zenith_rfi_completed.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet); gpu_fitment_matrix.pdf (application/pdf); commitment_scenarios.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument-spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Nora Singh <nora.singh@zenith-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing + GPU mix for inference workloads

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifications before the workshop:
- Can you show per-GPU expected QPS for our three model classes (13B / 34B / 70B) using the quantization levels you recommend? Numeric ops per second or stable QPS numbers help our capacity committee.
- For burst: how quickly can Redwood spin up the extra 1.8x capacity and what is the expected cold-start impact?
- Fallback model variants: if H100 capacity is saturated, do you have compatible lower-cost variants (e.g., 34B quantized on A100 or 13B on L4) with automatic routing?

Would also like the latency p95 numbers you modeled for both steady baseline and peak burst.

Best,
Nora
Sr. Cloud Procurement — Zenith Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood-inference.com, irene_choi@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-09-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing + GPU mix for inference workloads — quick internal alignment

Folks — forwarding Nora's follow-up. Quick thoughts and what I'd like us to confirm before the workshop:

> From: Nora Singh — "Can you show per-GPU expected QPS for our three model classes (13B / 34B / 70B) using the quantization levels you recommend? Numeric ops per second or stable QPS numbers help our capacity committee."

Proposed short answers (we'll calibrate numbers in the workbook):
- 13B quantized 4-bit on L4/A10G: ~120–180 QPS per GPU for short-chat-style requests (85 tokens).
- 34B quantized 4/8-bit on A100-80GB: ~40–70 QPS per GPU.
- 70B optimized on H100 (FP8/AMP + kernel optimizations): ~18–28 QPS per GPU.

Cold-start / burst behavior:
- We can spin additional instances within ~2–6 minutes for full node spin-up depending on cloud image cache; warm standby (pre-provisioned) reduces to <45s for container start. We should recommend a small warm pool for predictable peak windows.

Fallback routing:
- Yes — our smart routing allows policy-based fallback to compatible quantized variants on A100s or L4s. We can define per-endpoint routing policies (latency-priority vs cost-priority).

Requesting Monica: please validate the per-GPU QPS numbers in the GPU_fitment_matrix.pdf (you own the microbench numbers). Irene: can you call out operational notes for warm standby / cold start and exact autoscale timings we should present?

Thanks — I'll incorporate your confirmations into a short slide for the workshop.

— Karthik

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@zenith-analytics.com>, Nora Singh <nora.singh@zenith-analytics.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood-inference.com, monica_patel@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-09-07T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing + GPU mix for inference workloads — confirmed numbers and next steps

Hi Nora / Liam —

Following an internal calibration, attached is an updated matrix with conservative per-GPU QPS and expected p95 latencies (steady vs peak). Summary of the confirmed balanced scenario we recommend for your 12-month reservation:

- Reserved baseline: 8 x H100 (70B heavy), 18 x A100-80GB (34B/mid), 22 x L4/A10G (embeddings and small models).
- Modeled steady-state p95 latencies: Chat (13B/34B): 120–200ms; 70B chat on H100: 160–240ms. Embeddings p95 on L4: 30–60ms.
- Per-GPU conservative QPS (85-token requests): 13B on L4/A10G = 100 QPS; 34B on A100 = 50 QPS; 70B on H100 = 20 QPS. These conservative numbers assume mixed request sizes and include a 10% safety margin.
- Burst/Autoscale: recommend warm standby of 10% of burst capacity (reduces cold-start to <60s) with on-demand nodes available to reach full 1.8x within ~4–6 minutes.
- Routing & fallbacks: automatic routing policies will fallback 70B requests to 34B quantized variants (if acceptable to the application) or route to A100s if H100s are congested. We can expose per-endpoint policy toggles so your engineers control cost vs quality behavior.

Attachments: updated_gpu_fitment_matrix.pdf (includes per-GPU microbench numbers and p95 curves), commitment_scenarios_v2.xlsx (pricing bands), workshop_agenda.docx

Next steps:
1) Confirm you want us to schedule a 90-minute sizing workshop (we suggest Tuesday 2026-09-14 10:00–11:30 PT).
2) Let us know which commitment scenario you'd like us to price (conservative/balanced/aggressive).
3) Provide any additional compliance questions for the contract team — we can have legal join the workshop if needed.

I'll post the Drive folder with the updated artifacts to the HubSpot record and share the workshop invitation once we lock time.

Best regards,
